rule: After selective restore, ALWAYS re-run the FULL pytest suite (pytest app/tests/ -q -p no:cacheprovider) to confirm the regression is actually gone. Do not assume reverting the file returns to baseline-green.
why: iter-6 reverted _shared.py but the workflow never re-verified after checkout; 'restore succeeded' was an assumption. iter-5 showed restore can leave a still-red suite when the post-verify runs only a subset.

rule: The restore record carries the ACTUAL filesReverted (from the git checkout action). Pass that exact list into the report; the report must state the reverted files VERBATIM and must never infer or guess which file was reverted.
why: iter-6 report said 'reverted the risky require_ffmpeg change' when require_ffmpeg had actually SURVIVED — the report LLM guessed because only the count was passed, not the names.

rule: restoreTriggered:true is NOT a success signal on its own. Treat any restore as 'needs independent verification' and surface the post-restore pytest result in the report.
why: Across iters, restoreTriggered coexisted with both fully-green and still-red trees; the flag only means 'a revert was attempted'.

rule: When a fix changes a value's None-ness (e.g. `val or default` -> explicit `is None` check), grep EVERY downstream consumer of that variable for unguarded use and add the needed guard in the SAME fix. If a consumer cannot be guarded here, mark the fix 'skipped' with the reason rather than ship a crash.
why: iter-6 changed `count or 1`->None-check at the assignment site but seed_sequence received count=None with no guard -> real crash -> regression -> reverted. The sentinel fix is incomplete at the assignment site alone.

rule: except over-reach is the #1 error-handling fix defect. Narrow catches to the specific exception. A missing binary (FileNotFoundError) is an environment error that must stay LOUD — propagate it, or degrade WITH a stderr warning; never silence it.
why: iter-5 audio_noise_detect caught FileNotFoundError, hiding a missing-ffmpeg env error that the test contract required to propagate.

rule: A finding can have a REAL symptom but the WRONG root-cause location. When a finding blames file X, chase the symptom to its real offender before fixing X.
why: A HIGH finding blamed image-profile.py's --seed default=None sentinel (correct/intended); the real bug was two consumers doing `args.seed % (2**32)` without a None-guard.

rule: A finding's symptom can be entirely FABRICATED. For any finding claiming a runtime behavior ('X silently does Y'), trace the ACTUAL code path to confirm the behavior can happen at all before judging the fix.
why: iter-4 HIGH finding claimed run.py animate 'silently dispatches the WRONG model'; animate was in neither COMMAND_NAMES nor ALIASES and the dispatcher uses required subparsers -> argparse rejects unknown commands. No dispatch occurs. Adversarial verify UPHELD it (1/1) — re-deriving plausibility from the same flawed premise.

rule: Findings that mis-state a language/protocol primitive are a false-positive class: e.g. '__exit__ does not run if the body raises' (it always runs — that's the context-manager contract), 'finally is skipped', 'the decorator bypasses X'. Verify the primitive actually behaves as the finding claims.
why: iter-6 flagged GpuLock __exit__ fd-leak on a false premise; the workflow correctly added only annotations. The adversarial verifier cannot catch these (same flawed premise).

rule: Report recommendations must reflect the ACTUAL final tree state (git diff --stat), never assumptions about what was reverted. If a recommendation says 're-attempt X', first confirm X is not already in the tree.
why: iter-6 recommendation #5 said 're-attempt require_ffmpeg' but require_ffmpeg had already shipped that run — the rec was stale because it trusted the (wrong) restore narrative.
